This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 531/2024 registered at Police Station,
Deendayal Nagar District Ratlam (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n)
of IPC and Sections 5(J-11)/6 of POCSO Act.

Police Station,
Deendayal Nagar District Ratlam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in judicial custody since 19.12.2024.
As per the case of prosecution, the victim aged 17 years 01 month went missing on 22.06.2024.
Father of the victim reported that some unknown person has enticed and taken his daughter.

P.S.
Deendayal Nagar District Ratlam registered FIR for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against unknown person.
The victim was recovered from possession of child in conflict with law.
In her statement recorded u/S 160 and 164 of Cr.P.C., victim stated that her parents had married NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6837 2 MCRC-6351-2025 her with Jitendra .
She did not like Jitendra.
Jitendra used to ill-treat her.

She had liking for child in conflict with law,
therefore, she went with him to Indore.
On such statement Jitendra was apprehended for offence punishable u/S 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sec 5(J-11)/6 of POCSO on 19.12.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
Victim was sent for medico legal examination.
On medical examination, the victim was found pregnant for 15 weeks and 02 days.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.

The parents of the victim had married Jitendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168441477/

sentences.text: Victim and the child in conflict with law reside at Indore for one month.
They had physical relations.
The determination of age of victim during investigation is doubtful.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
Applicant is aged 19 years.
He is a labourer by profession and dependent on family.
No criminal antecedents is reported against the applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6837 3 MCRC-6351-2025 Heard the arguments,
perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
The case diary and material on record reveals that parents of the victim had married her to applicant, but victim eloped with her friend, the child in conflict with law.
Victim and the child in conflict with law stayed in Indore for almost a month.
They had physical relations.
Except omnibus statement of victim, no incriminating evidence is available on record against the applicant.
The veracity of the prosecution will be considered in evidence during trial.
As per information, applicant is aged around 19 years.
He is a labourer by profession and is dependent on his family.
Considering the age and family status of applicant, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant and the complainant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.

However, it is clarified that the observations,
herein above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Jitendra shall be released NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6837 4 MCRC-6351-2025 on bail in connection with the Crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973 / Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.

2 he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules.
